title: Number of Balanced Integers in a Range
summary: Given two integers low and high, count the balanced integers within the range [low, high].
statement: Given two integers low and high, count the balanced integers within the range [low, high]. An integer is balanced if it has at least two digits and the sum of digits in even positions equals the sum of digits in odd positions.
constraints: A balanced integer has at least two digits.
Positions count from one at the left; odd-position and even-position digit sums must match.
hints: Count valid values up to a bound, then subtract the count below low.
Digit DP tracks position, alternating-sum difference, and whether the prefix is tight to the bound.
Add a digit to the difference at even zero-based positions and subtract it at odd positions; accept final difference zero.
Leading zero padding may swap parity for shorter lengths but equality with zero is invariant under sign, while removing the all-zero value enforces at least two digits after starting at 11.
editorial: Leading zero padding may swap parity for shorter lengths but equality with zero is invariant under sign, while removing the all-zero value enforces at least two digits after starting at 11.

tests.explanation: The balanced values are 11,22,…,99, for a total of nine.
Only 121 has equal odd- and even-position digit sums.
